CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Kepahiang Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Kepahiang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are autonomous authority.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence occurring in the Kepahiang Regency area.
10. Protection of women and children is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence starting from prevention, handling, recovery and empowerment.
11. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against the victim.
12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out the function of integrated services for the protection of women and child victims of violence.
14. Safe House is a residence for victims, during the process of assistance, and recovery for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and actions of perpetrators.
15. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints, identification, health and psychological recovery, legal services up to the returning and reintegration of victims into society.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Household is husband, wife, and children, and people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the APBD of Kepahiang Regency.

Article 35

1. In the event of being caught red-handed as referred to in Article 33 letter d, the community may secure the perpetrator before handing them over to the authorities.
2. The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 28 letters b and e are that they legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as family members.
3. The role of the community as referred to in Article 34 paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, child protection institutions, community social institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.

Article 13

Other violence as referred to in Article 7 letter (f) is caused by:

a. threat of violence includes any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered or forced to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER V

P2TP2A

Article 38

1. The Regional Government in order to provide services and protection to women and children victims of acts of violence shall form P2TP2A.
2. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) constitutes a functional work unit having the duties, main tasks, and functions of providing integrated protection to women and children from acts of violence.

CHAPTER VII

SAFE HOUSE

Article 46

1. A safe house must be provided by the Social Service to handle cases of violence against women and children that pose a high risk to the safety of victims.
2. The management of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) refers to the applicable laws and regulations.
3. The financing of the management of the Safe House as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be charged to the Regional Budget.

CHAPTER XI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 50

1. The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. forming family partners at the Village/Sub-district level;
b. forming women and child protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, and mass media.

Article 4

The scope of protection of women and children includes prevention, service, recovery and empowerment efforts.

CHAPTER III

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Part One

Prevention

ELUCIDATION OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY

NUMBER 10 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

AGAINST VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Sociologically, violence against women and children has been increasing both quantitatively and qualitatively. This is in line with technological developments that can be imitated by perpetrators of violence at any time, so that the quality is also increasing. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who work and live on plantations often neglect their attention and responsibility towards their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

Article 12

Exploitation as referred to in Article 7 letter (e) is caused by:

a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse

Paragraph 1

Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

Article 8

Physical violence as referred to in Article 7 letter (a) is caused by acts or physical actions that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse

Article 13

a. threat of violence includes any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and

Article 24

Forms of empowerment of women victims of violence include:

a. job training;
b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups; and
c. capital assistance.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation.

Sociologically, violence against women and children has been increasing both quantitatively and qualitatively. This is in line with technological developments that can be imitated by perpetrators of violence at any time, so that the quality is also increasing. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who work and live on plantations often neglect their attention and responsibility towards their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

AGAINST VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Sociologically, violence against women and children has been increasing both quantitatively and qualitatively. This is in line with technological developments that can be imitated by perpetrators of violence at any time, so that the quality is also increasing. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who work and live on plantations often neglect their attention and responsibility towards their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Kepahiang Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Kepahiang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are autonomous authority.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence occurring in the Kepahiang Regency area.
10. Protection of women and children is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence starting from prevention, handling, recovery and empowerment.
11. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against the victim.
12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out the function of integrated services for the protection of women and child victims of violence.
14. Safe House is a residence for victims, during the process of assistance, and recovery for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and actions of perpetrators.
15. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints, identification, health and psychological recovery, legal services up to the returning and reintegration of victims into society.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Household is husband, wife, and children, and people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the APBD of Kepahiang Regency.

CHAPTER XI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 50

1. The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.

c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, and mass media.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

10. Protection of women and children is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence starting from prevention, handling, recovery and empowerment.

16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Household is husband, wife, and children, and people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

AGAINST VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Sociologically, violence against women and children has been increasing both quantitatively and qualitatively. This is in line with technological developments that can be imitated by perpetrators of violence at any time, so that the quality is also increasing. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who work and live on plantations often neglect their attention and responsibility towards their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

CHAPTER XI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 50

1. The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. forming family partners at the Village/Sub-district level;
b. forming women and child protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, and mass media.

Article 35

1. In the event of being caught red-handed as referred to in Article 33 letter d, the community may secure the perpetrator before handing them over to the authorities.
2. The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 28 letters b and e are that they legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as family members.
3. The role of the community as referred to in Article 34 paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, child protection institutions, community social institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Kepahiang Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Kepahiang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are autonomous authority.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence occurring in the Kepahiang Regency area.
10. Protection of women and children is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence starting from prevention, handling, recovery and empowerment.
11. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against the victim.
12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out the function of integrated services for the protection of women and child victims of violence.
14. Safe House is a residence for victims, during the process of assistance, and recovery for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and actions of perpetrators.
15. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints, identification, health and psychological recovery, legal services up to the returning and reintegration of victims into society.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Household is husband, wife, and children, and people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the APBD of Kepahiang Regency.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

AGAINST VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Sociologically, violence against women and children has been increasing both quantitatively and qualitatively. This is in line with technological developments that can be imitated by perpetrators of violence at any time, so that the quality is also increasing. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who work and live on plantations often neglect their attention and responsibility towards their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups. Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of the victim" is that all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

ELUCIDATION OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY

NUMBER 10 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

AGAINST VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Sociologically, violence against women and children has been increasing both quantitatively and qualitatively. This is in line with technological developments that can be imitated by perpetrators of violence at any time, so that the quality is also increasing. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who work and live on plantations often neglect their attention and responsibility towards their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men, including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups. Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of the victim" is that all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

ELUCIDATION OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY

NUMBER 10 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

AGAINST VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Sociologically, violence against women and children has been increasing both quantitatively and qualitatively. This is in line with technological developments that can be imitated by perpetrators of violence at any time, so that the quality is also increasing. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who work and live on plantations often neglect their attention and responsibility towards their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

REGENT OF KEPAHIANG

DECIDES:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

ELUCIDATION OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY

NUMBER 10 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

AGAINST VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Sociologically, violence against women and children has been increasing both quantitatively and qualitatively. This is in line with technological developments that can be imitated by perpetrators of violence at any time, so that the quality is also increasing. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who work and live on plantations often neglect their attention and responsibility towards their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse

P2TP2A

Article 38

1. The Regional Government in order to provide services and protection to women and children victims of acts of violence shall form P2TP2A.

Article 23

1. Return and reintegration services into society as referred to in Article 17 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment.

Article 35

1. In the event of being caught red-handed as referred to in Article 33 letter d, the community may secure the perpetrator before handing them over to the authorities.
2. The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 28 letters b and e are that they legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as family members.
3. The role of the community as referred to in Article 34 paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, child protection institutions, community social institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.

CHAPTER XI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 50

1. The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. forming family partners at the Village/Sub-district level;
b. forming women and child protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, and mass media.

ELUCIDATION OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY

NUMBER 10 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

AGAINST VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.

Sociologically, violence against women and children has been increasing both quantitatively and qualitatively. This is in line with technological developments that can be imitated by perpetrators of violence at any time, so that the quality is also increasing. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who work and live on plantations often neglect their attention and responsibility towards their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.
